punchline: Elizabeth Gilbert lets fear ride along on every project, but never lets it drive.
thirty_sec: In Big Magic, Elizabeth Gilbert admits she feels fear before every project. Instead of waiting for it to go, she speaks to it like a passenger on a road trip: it can come along and have a voice, but it can't drive, touch the maps or suggest detours. She calls perfectionism 'fear in fancy shoes and a mink coat,' and repeats her mother's motto: done is better than good.
question: What would you do if your fear had a seat but no say?
